Modern architecture reflects our collective psyche. Glass and steel towers, each indistinguishable from the last. Efficiency prioritized over beauty. Function divorced from meaning.

I visited a building from the 1920s last Tuesday. The craftsmanship was staggering. Every detail considered, every element serving both practical and aesthetic purposes. The architects understood something we've forgotten: spaces shape the people who inhabit them.

Compare this to contemporary office buildings. Fluorescent lighting, identical cubicles, windows that don't open. These environments don't support human flourishing. They optimize for productivity, measured in narrow, quantifiable terms. We've traded well-being for efficiency, and the cost is higher than we acknowledge.
